question: In Python, an if-statement can be used to execute a block of code if a specified condition is true.
The syntax of an if-statement in Python always requires a colon at the end of the condition.
In Python, an if-statement can only check for equality conditions.
An if-statement in Python can have multiple elif parts to check additional conditions.
If-statements in Python require an else part.
Python if-statements can only compare integer values.
The following code will cause an error: 'if True print('yes'):'.
The else part of an if-else structure executes when the if condition is true.
In Python, nested if-statements allow you to place an if-statement inside another if-statement.
The expression inside an if-statement's condition must always return a boolean value.
